SEARCH

All Classes and Interfaces

Class
Description
AiProvider
The AI backends AiScriptService can talk to.
AiScriptService
Turns a plain-English instruction into a bash script using an OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions API.
ArchiveService
Lists and extracts common archive formats.
ConvertDialog
The "Convert" dialog: turns pasted text, a local file, or a URL — in CSV, TSV, JSON, XML, Markdown-table, YAML, or Excel (.xlsx) format — into SQL (for a choice of SQLite, MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle, or Microsoft SQL Server), CSV, TSV, JSON, XML, an HTML table, a Markdown table, YAML, or Excel, inspired by convertcsv.com.
CsvTableWriter
Renders a TableData as standard comma-separated CSV text, quoting only the fields that need it (containing a comma, double quote, or line break) and doubling any embedded quotes — the same convention DelimitedTableParser reads back.
CustomFolder
A user-added bookmark/shortcut folder shown in the left panel, persisted in SQLite.
Database
Owns the ~/.dfiles/dfiles.sqlite file used to persist bookmarks, app settings, per-folder view preferences, saved AI-assisted bash scripts, and a filesystem cache that lets folders paint instantly on repeat visits (the real listing is refreshed right after, in the background).
DelimitedTableParser
Parses CSV and TSV text into a TableData, treating the first line as the header row.
DesktopOpener
Opens a file with the operating system's registered default application for its type.
DirectoryScanner
Reads a directory's entries off the JavaFX Application Thread.
FileItem
A single row shown in the right-hand file table: one filesystem entry.
FileSizeFormatter
 
FileTablePane
Right-hand panel: sortable table of the current folder's contents.
FileTypeUtil
Maps file extensions to a human-readable type label and a small emoji glyph used as a stand-in icon.
FolderWatcherService
Watches one directory at a time on a background daemon thread and notifies the UI (via Platform.runLater) whenever entries are created, removed or modified, so the currently open folder stays live without the user hitting refresh.
GitService
Thin wrapper that shells out to the `git` command line for the folder currently being browsed.
GitService.GitResult
 
HtmlTableWriter
Renders a TableData as a standalone HTML <table> with a <thead> header row and one <tbody> row per record, escaping every cell's text content.
I18n
Small wrapper around ResourceBundle for the app's five supported locales.
JsonTableParser
Parses a JSON array of flat objects (or a single JSON object, treated as one row) into a TableData.
JsonTableWriter
Renders a TableData as a pretty-printed JSON array of objects — the same shape JsonTableParser reads back.
LatinCsvConverter
Converts a "Latin" (continental European) CSV file — ; as the field separator and , as the decimal mark, e.g.
Launcher
Separate entry point (does not extend javafx.application.Application) so the app can be run as a plain runnable jar without the JVM's "JavaFX runtime components are missing" launcher check, which only inspects the declared main class.
LeftPane
Left-hand navigation panel: standard "places" plus user-defined bookmarked folders.
MainApp
 
MainController
Glues the left places panel, the file table, the toolbar and all background services together.
MarkdownTableParser
Parses a GitHub-Flavored-Markdown pipe table (the kind rendered by GitHub, GitLab, and most Markdown editors) into a TableData.
MarkdownTableWriter
Renders a TableData as a GitHub-Flavored-Markdown pipe table, the same shape MarkdownTableParser reads.
PlaceEntry
An entry rendered in the left places panel: either a built-in standard folder or a user bookmark.
PlaceEntry.Kind
 
PosixInfoFormatter
Renders a single file's metadata the way `ls -l` would, e.g.
ScriptDetails
The full saved state of one script: the AI prompt (if any) that produced it, its bash content, the output captured the last time it was run and tested, a SHA-256 hash of the content that changes whenever the script is edited, and the epoch-millisecond timestamps of when it was first created and last saved.
ScriptDevPane
Tab 2 content: an AI-assisted bash script workspace split into three mouse-resizable rows — a prompt sent to an LLM (with a choice of AI backend), the resulting or hand-edited script, and a terminal-style view of running it.
ScriptEntry
A named bash script stored in the database, shown in the left panel's Scripts section.
ScriptRunner
Runs a bash script from a background thread, streaming its combined stdout/stderr back line by line via a ScriptRunner.Listener that is always invoked on the JavaFX Application Thread.
ScriptRunner.Listener
Callback for a running script's output and completion, invoked on the FX Application Thread.
ScriptSaveResult
The values a script save recomputes: its new content hash and the timestamp the save was recorded at, returned together so the UI can refresh both without a second database query.
SqlDialect
A target SQL database for SqlTableWriter.
SqlTableWriter
Renders a TableData as SQL for a specific SqlDialect: an optional "drop table if it exists, then create it" pair (spelled however that dialect requires) with an inferred column type per column, then the data wrapped in a transaction.
TableConverter
Facade for the Convert feature: given raw input bytes, a text encoding, an input format (or TableInputFormat.AUTO to sniff one), and an output format, produces the converted result.
TableData
A generic in-memory table — column names plus rows of string cell values — used as the common intermediate form for the Convert feature: every supported input format (CSV, TSV, JSON, Markdown table, YAML, XLSX) is parsed into a TableData, and every supported output format (SQL, CSV) is written from one.
TableInputFormat
Formats TableConverter can parse into a TableData.
TableOutputFormat
Formats TableConverter can write a TableData out as.
TerminalLauncher
Opens a terminal emulator window at a given directory, trying common Linux/macOS/Windows terminals in turn.
TextPreviewService
Reads the first and last N lines of a text file without loading the whole thing into memory — the head comes from a normal line-by-line read that stops early, and the tail comes from seeking near the end of the file and only decoding that trailing chunk.
TextPreviewService.Preview
 
TsvTableWriter
Renders a TableData as tab-separated text, the same no-quoting convention DelimitedTableParser.parseTsv(java.lang.String) reads back — a cell containing a literal tab or line break isn't escaped, matching how TSV is conventionally produced.
VSCodeLauncher
Opens a folder in Visual Studio Code via its `code` CLI (installed on PATH by VS Code itself on Windows/Linux, or via "Shell Command: Install 'code' command in PATH" on macOS).
XlsxTableParser
Reads the first sheet of an .xlsx workbook into a TableData via Apache POI, treating the first non-empty row as the header.
XlsxTableWriter
Writes a TableData out as a real .xlsx workbook (one sheet, header row plus data rows) via Apache POI.
XmlTableParser
Parses an XML document shaped like repeated records — most commonly the same shape XmlTableWriter produces, e.g.
XmlTableWriter
Renders a TableData as XML — a <table> root containing one <row> per record, each with one child element per column — using the JDK's built-in XMLStreamWriter (StAX) rather than hand-built strings, so text content is always correctly escaped.
YamlTableParser
Parses the one YAML shape that maps naturally onto a table — a sequence of flat mappings, the same "list of records" pattern JSON uses for tabular data:
YamlTableWriter
Renders a TableData as the "list of flat mappings" YAML shape YamlTableParser reads back — one --prefixed block per row, one key: value line per column.
